items.followUp: Name the two main types of computer memory and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the two main categories of computer memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both categories.

rubric.why: Examples show understanding of the memory categories.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of computer memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one or more suitable examples.

modelAnswer: The two main types of computer memory are primary memory and secondary memory.
Examples include RAM and ROM (primary memory), and a hard disk (secondary memory).

items.followUp: State the two Identity Laws of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: One correct identity law is required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either A + 0 = A or A · 1 = A.

rubric.why: Both Boolean identity laws complete the answer.
rubric.how: Award the second mark when both laws are stated.

modelAnswer: The Identity Laws are A + 0 = A and A · 1 = A.

items.followUp: Name the three basic logical operators and write their symbols.

rubric.why: The basic logical operators are AND, OR, and NOT.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming AND, OR, and NOT.

rubric.why: Logical operators work on logical values and produce a logical result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they operate on logical values or conditions and produce a logical result.

modelAnswer: Logical operators are operators used to combine or modify logical conditions.
The basic logical operators are AND, OR, and NOT; they produce a true or false result.

items.followUp: Use a truth table to prove that A + B = B + A.

rubric.why: For equal inputs, both sides of the equation have equal outputs.
rubric.description: Shows the correct results for A = B (rows 00 and 11).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct outputs in both equal-input rows.

rubric.why: For different inputs, both sides also have equal outputs, proving commutativity.
rubric.description: Shows the correct results for A ≠ B (rows 01 and 10), or clearly concludes the columns are equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct outputs in both different-input rows and the equality of the result columns.

modelAnswer: A B | A · B | B · A
The output columns are identical; therefore, A · B = B · A.

items.followUp: Define a network protocol and give one example.

rubric.why: A protocol establishes rules for communication.
rubric.description: Identifies a protocol as a set of rules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a set of rules.

rubric.why: The rules govern communication or data exchange over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the rules to communication or data transmission between network devices.

modelAnswer: A network protocol is a set of rules that governs communication and data transmission between devices on a network.

items.followUp: State one advantage of Star Topology.

rubric.why: The disadvantage relates to the central connecting device.
rubric.description: Identifies the central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the central device.

rubric.why: Failure of the central device can interrupt the whole network.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of central-device failure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that failure of the hub or switch can bring down the network.

modelAnswer: The major disadvantage of Star Topology is that if its central hub or switch fails, the entire network may stop working.

items.followUp: What is a point-to-point connection? Give one example.

rubric.why: A point-to-point connection links two endpoints directly.
rubric.description: Describes the direct link between endpoints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a direct connection or link.

rubric.why: The example must show two devices connected directly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as two computers connected directly by a cable.

modelAnswer: A point-to-point connection is a direct link between two devices.
For example, two computers connected directly by a cable form a point-to-point connection.

items.followUp: What is a software product key, and what is its purpose?

rubric.why: A software key is a code associated with a software licence.
rubric.description: Identifies the software key as a code or serial number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a product or activation code.

rubric.why: The key is used to authenticate or activate licensed software; unauthorized copying or use is piracy.
rubric.description: Explains its use and its connection to piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the key is used to install, activate, or verify licensed software and that unauthorized use is piracy.

modelAnswer: A software key is a unique product or activation code supplied with software.
Using or copying a software key without authorization to install or activate software is software piracy.
